confirmed: Source checked: abstract only (OpenAlex abstract_inverted_index and Semantic Scholar API, identical text independently retrieved and read in full on 2026-10-09), plus Crossref bibliographic metadata. The form correctly labels its evidence as abstract only. OpenAlex: https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1145/3772363.3799384; Semantic Scholar: https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/DOI:10.1145/3772363.3799384?fields=title,abstract; Crossref: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/3772363.3799384.

Full-text limitation: retrieval.json records c090 as not_obtained; no markdown or PDF was supplied. The publisher PDF request returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-09 (https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3772363.3799384). OpenAlex lists only the publisher location; the arXiv API query all:AHAlogy returned zero records. No full text, PDF page, table, figure, or appendix was inspected.

Title, five authors (Lu Liu, Wenjia Tan, Yi Zhao, Jianhui Pang, Derek F. Wong), DOI, and publication in the Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference are confirmed by Crossref title, author, container-title, and DOI fields at the API URL above.

The abstract describes a five-day between-subjects classroom study reporting N = 38 elementary-school students aged 7–11; 38 counts people, not texts, ideas, or ratings, and is below the 50-person threshold (abstract, sentence 3).

AHAlogy is a curriculum-aligned LLM agent used in class; the Control receives curriculum only and the Experimental group receives curriculum plus AHAlogy (abstract, sentences 2–3). The abstract does not name the underlying model.

Random assignment, assignment unit, and arm sizes are not stated (entire abstract, especially sentence 3). Thus design_class=other, assignment.randomized=not_stated, criterion_1=unclear, and context_class=none are defensible provisional codes; neither randomized nor nonrandom assignment is established. has_randomized_people_study=false here means no randomized people study was confirmed from the accessible evidence, not proof that assignment was nonrandom.

The verbatim excerpts in all three reported fields match the independently retrieved abstract. It reports significant Time × Group interactions and larger Experimental-group gains for fluency and flexibility, and says originality did not significantly change (abstract, sentence 5).

The one-line finding accurately repeats the reported duration, sample, ages, and qualitative findings (abstract, sentences 3 and 5). Its phrase about no numbers should be understood as no numerical effect estimates or inferential statistics: the abstract does contain N and ages, but no means, standard deviations, effect sizes, confidence intervals, test statistics, or numerical p values (entire abstract).

The accessible source describes one comparative classroom study and no synthesis or pooled estimate; the synthesis fields appropriately remain empty (abstract, sentences 2–7). Core inclusion is not established, consistent with eligibility.core=no and the reported sample below 50; output-scoring eligibility still needs methods.
summary: The abstract confirms the reported sample of 38 and qualitative findings, but several coded fields exceed its evidence. Randomization remains unconfirmed; analyzed count, AI removal, timing, scoring, analysis unit, and the originality between-group contrast require full text.
